Interviewer:	Thank you for agreeing to see me. It’s the Sound Technology course that you’re on isn’t it?

Subject:	Yes.

Interviewer:	Did you do A levels?

Subject:	In [country] in secondary school, it’s quite different the system there.

Interviewer:	Ok what type of school did you go to?

Subject:	Just a normal mixed school.

Interviewer:	It wasn’t a girls school or anything?

Subject:	No, no.

Interviewer:	Ok, have you got any previous experience in your industry?

Subject:	No. Nothing at all.

Interviewer:	Ok, what do your parents do? Do they do anything similar to the course that you’re doing?

Subject:	Quite different, my parents, my father is an engineer, but civil engineering so, its different from what I’m doing. My mother she studied economics so.

Interviewer:	When and why then, do you think that you decided to do sound technology?

Subject:	Erm, like when I was in my second year of secondary school I started to be more interested in audio visual kind of engineering studies. Yes, so I decided to come and. First of all, when I enrolled, I wanted to go to media, media technology, but then I changed to sound. I like them both.

Interviewer:	What sort of things is it about media and sound technology that you like?

Subject:	Er, I love like image. I think that now that I’m on my final year I find out that I like, that I prefer the part of video than the sound. That’s why if I’m going to do a master, I’m going to change it to video. But I love it, I love image and er you know, trying to modify it and to do whatever I want.

Interviewer:	Before you came to university did you do any career research to see what jobs were available afterwards or anything like that?

Subject:	No, I did before secondary school yes. But not before I come to university. I decided I wanted this and 

Interviewer:	You thought you’d enjoy the course?

Subject:	Yes.

Interviewer:	Ok, why did you decide to come to [university]?

Subject:	Because I had a cousin studying here and I wanted to try to have the experience of studying outside [country], and my cousin was studying here so I just came.

Interviewer:	Ok, is your degree mainly male or female students?

Subject:	Male. It’s me and another girl are the only girls.

Interviewer:	Did you realise that before you started?

Subject:	I knew, I knew that there would be more girls than boys, but not a big difference, but I knew, I was prepared.

Interviewer:	Did that bother you at all?

Subject:	No, not at all because I think I’m used to dealing with boys, so not at all.

Interviewer:	Do you think that more women should be encouraged to do engineering or sound technology?

Subject:	Yes, definitely. I think a lot of women like this area, but they don’t go because they feel bothered to know that they are going to study only with men and yes they just don’t take the risk.

Interviewer:	What do you think could be done to get more women involved?

Subject:	Encouragement, I don’t know. I’m on a poster from my school now and three girls. We are three girls working in a studio. I think if other girls see it and see oh there are some girls studying that, I think I can go. I think encouragement yes.

Interviewer:	Ok. What characteristics do you think make a good sound engineer? Do you think you need a certain type of personality?

Subject:	I don’t know. I think it’s the same as other areas actually like, know how to work in a group, because sometimes you will need to work in a group. Er, know how to work individually, like have responsibility, to know what you have to do and do it on time and I don’t know.

Interviewer:	Do you think that there are any advantages or disadvantages to being a woman in engineering?

Subject:	Er yes I do think because it’s easier. I think they expect more from a guy than from a girl. I don’t know why because they’re more used to seeing guys in these areas perhaps, and er, I think a girl has to be really really good to get something.

Interviewer:	How does that make you feel?

Subject:	Er, I’m optimistic, I’m optimistic. And I hope I will be really good.

Interviewer:	Ok, has your degree been what you expected it to be so far?

Subject:	I er. At the beginning I thought that on my third year I’d have more experience. I’d be better prepared for the working in industry, but I don’t feel like it. That’s why I’m anxious to do some work, to have some work placement or something to have that confidence. I don’t have any confidence. I think on like the thing of being prepared, I’m not afraid, you know, I want to try, but I’m not ready yet.

Interviewer:	Do you think there is anything the university could do to help prepare you more?

Subject:	Erm, to help prepare …

Interviewer:	To prepare you for going out in industry? Or do you think you just need to go and get experience?

Subject:	No I think the course is sometimes not well structured. We miss a lot of time on modules that I think that are not as much important as. If we spent more time like on practical, on the practical side of the course, I think it would be better, like more studio time, in my case.

Interviewer:	I’ll may be talk a bit more about that in a bit, but what would you say have been the best and worst things about the course?

Subject:	Ah, the best, ah I don’t know. The worst thing I think is right now on my final project, I have to work with six more guys and its kind of difficult because it’s my final project and its not depending only on me, its depending on six other people and sometimes they don’t work as you want them to work. And it’s a bit messy and so I’m a bit worried about it.

Interviewer:	Do you think that doing group work is a good idea though?

Subject:	I think it’s a good idea because when I, on my future I’ll be working on teams, but not such big teams for this kind of project. It’s like, it’s a small project so on the reality, it would be a small team as well, and this team its too big. But I think on the other hand if the projects were individually I think it would be good as well, because they would be able to mark, to evaluate a student you know, with more precision.

Interviewer:	Have you been taught by any female lecturers at all?

Subject:	Yes. Yes, my first and my second year. But not technical modules, no. the technical ones are always by men.

Interviewer:	So you have noticed a clear difference between them?

Subject:	Yes.

Interviewer:	Ok, do you think that the male and female lecturers have a different style of teaching as well?

Subject:	Erm, no I don’t think it depends on the sex.

Interviewer:	Would you find it encouraging to have female lecturers on the female side?

Subject:	I think if we had female lecturers, yes it would be good.

Interviewer:	Do you think that the female lecturers treat you the same as the male lecturers?

Subject:	Yes, I do. I don’t feel that much difference, just because I’m a girl. They don’t treat me in a special way or something, no. I’m like the others.

Interviewer:	Have you got a personal tutor?

Subject:	I do but I just met him in my first year, and no more.

Interviewer:	Do you think it is a good idea to have a personal tutor?

Subject:	I think so. I think I should like go and talk to him sometimes, but I just didn’t and its too late now. But I do talk with some of my lecturers, but I don’t have that kind of relationship with my personal tutor, but yes with my other lecturers I do.

Interviewer:	Do you think it would have been different if you’d had a different personal tutor?

Subject:	Yes I think so, because he’s not my lecturer. He’s never been, he’s from my school, but not from my area, so that doesn’t help me.

Interviewer:	Ok. Is there anything, or anyone, that you would say has been the biggest influence on you since you started the course?

Subject:	Erm, I think myself. I decided to come here.

Interviewer:	Could you have gone on placement while you were at university?

Subject:	Yes, last. This year I could be on placement.

Interviewer:	And why did you decide not to do it?

Subject:	Because I want to finish this and yes I think it would be difficult to come back and start studying again and to finish it. So I want to finish it first and then try and go into the industry.

Interviewer:	Do you think that there are any advantages to doing a placement?

Subject:	I think so because I know some guys they’ve done it. And when they come to the third year, they’re more prepared to do tasks that they give us. Yeah I think so, its good.

Interviewer:	You said that you are thinking about doing a masters, is that because you are thinking about going into a different area, or are there any other reasons why you’d like to do it?

Subject:	Yes, because I want to change to video and because I want to specialise in the (addition?) part. I want to really have an intensive course and I think its good if you have a greater degree. Like you have your degree and then the great, I don’t know the word?

Interviewer:	A higher qualification?

Subject:	Yes I think it’s good and more work opportunities.

Interviewer:	Did you say that you might have a year out before you do that?

Subject:	No not at all. I’ll try to get a placement during the summer, but then in the next academic year I’ll be doing my masters.

Interviewer:	Have you looked at getting a placement yet?

Subject:	Yes, but not here, in [country], but I’m trying. I’m sending over my CV.

Interviewer:	Is it easier to get work there or are you going to stay with your family?

Subject:	Yes I just want to go back home.

Interviewer:	If you did want a placement here, is the university helpful, would they help you find a placement?

Subject:	They help us to find placements but I think in my area its very difficult. I went to some sections for this (finality?) they always talked about other areas and mine was a bit outside so, I don’t know. I think if they could, they would help us more than they do. But its really difficult to get work in this area.

Interviewer:	Do you know what type of company you think you’d like to work for when you finish?

Subject:	Er like er, production companies, publicity companies, yeah, or tv companies.

Interviewer:	Ok, do you know what sort of things will attract you to a company, or when you’ve been looking for a placement, have you been sending your CV to everyone or…

Subject:	I’ve been sending it to everyone but its like, if I could choose, only because I want the work experience now, but if I could chose, I’d chose like a dynamic company with a good working environment, a good team. I’d look at the image of the company as well, that’s very important I think.

Interviewer:	How do you think that being at work will differ from being at university?

Subject:	Like when you have an assignment in university you can decide oh I’m not going to do it today, I’m going to do it tomorrow, but when you’re working you have to be more responsible and, you know, have to be there and do it. Because they are paying you, it’s quite different. And when you are at university you are not expected to know everything, but when you’re working, I think they expect more from you because, yes.

Interviewer:	Ok, do you think that there is anything, apart from the technical skills that you are learning, do you think that there are any aspect of uni or any advice that you’ve had that will be particularly helpful when you start work?

Subject:	Like knowing different kinds of people. Like I’m here and I know people from all around the world. I’m quite like, I’m used to dealing with different types of people, I think it helps a lot like if I’m going to work with a team, I’ll be more able to integrate myself in the team and you know, I think the relationship will be better.

Interviewer:	So you think it has helped develop your interpersonal skills?

Subject:	Interpersonal skills, yes.

Interviewer:	What do you think will be the best and worst things about working in the industry?

Subject:	Er, the best thing I think the adrenalin. You have something to do, you have a production to make and then you make it and then you see the result. And the results will be seen by thousands of people, and that’s good. And the worst thing I think, in my area, we’ll have to work day and night, all day if its necessary. I think I’ll be, I’ll have some problems with that but just at the beginning not to have a schedule, a fixed schedule or something.

Interviewer:	In terms of your career then, what do you think you’ll be doing in five years time?

Subject:	Er, I’ll be a very successful video editor. Yes I’ll be doing what I want. My dream is to work in cinema, so I’ll be doing like working in the cinema and er doing my other projects, my side projects as well.

Interviewer:	Do you think that you will stay here and work or do you want to travel or go back home?

Subject:	I don’t know yet, I’m going to have my masters done and then I’ll see if I go back home or if I stay, it will depend on the job opportunities. I’d like to travel, yes I would, but I don’t know if it will be possible or not.

Interviewer:	Are you going to do your masters here?

Subject:	Erm, I’m deciding, I don’t know if I’m going to stay here in the UK, not in this university, but in the UK or Spain. I’m not sure yet.

Interviewer:	Are there many universities that do your course?

Subject:	Er in UK, yeah I think so. In London and in England actually.

Interviewer:	Ok, do you think that the career prospects are good in your area? Are there lots of job opportunities?

Subject:	I think it will be difficult at first. It’s like I don’t imagine me going and finding a beautiful job at first, but er I’ll have to fight and work really hard.

Interviewer:	Are you happy with all the career choices you’ve made so far? If you did it all over again would you do anything differently?

Subject:	Perhaps not going to sound technology but media technology as I’ve found out it’s what I like the most. But I like sound as well, but I prefer video. But yeah, I think I’m happy with my choices.

Interviewer:	You seem enthusiastic about it. If you had to describe the culture or characteristics of your industry, what five words would you use?

Subject:	Erm, it’s a male industry, er I think competitive. It’s dynamic I think, I like that. I don’t know.

Interviewer:	What do you think it is about it that makes it a male industry?

Subject:	I don’t know, I think its because until now, we only see, it’s not we only see, but most of the time we only see men working and that’s why we connect it to, we say it’s a male industry, because we see more men than women working on it.

Interviewer:	Do you think that the fact its so male dominated will cause you any problems at all in the future?

Subject:	I think if I wanted to work in sound I’d have more problems than on the video part. I think, I’m not sure because I’ll only see after I’m in the industry, I think so, yeah.

Interviewer:	My last question is, do you think that your educational experiences differ from other students say in social sciences or humanities?

Subject:	I think this university has a very good practical side of the course, all courses have a very good practical side. Actually I have some friends studying sciences and they usually go to the labs as well, so I think its similar, I don’t know.

Interviewer:	Ok that’s everything. Thank you very much for your help.

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Like knowing different kinds of people. Like I’m here and I know people from all around the world. I’m quite like, I’m used to dealing with different types of people, I think it helps a lot like if I’m going to work with a team, I’ll be more able to integrate myself in the team and you know, I think the relationship will be better.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: So you think it has helped develop your interpersonal skills?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Interpersonal skills, yes.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: What do you think will be the best and worst things about working in the industry?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Er, the best thing I think the adrenalin. You have something to do, you have a production to make and then you make it and then you see the result. And the results will be seen by thousands of people, and that’s good. And the worst thing I think, in my area, we’ll have to work day and night, all day if its necessary. I think I’ll be, I’ll have some problems with that but just at the beginning not to have a schedule, a fixed schedule or something.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: In terms of your career then, what do you think you’ll be doing in five years time?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Er, I’ll be a very successful video editor. Yes I’ll be doing what I want. My dream is to work in cinema, so I’ll be doing like working in the cinema and er doing my other projects, my side projects as well.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Do you think that you will stay here and work or do you want to travel or go back home?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: I don’t know yet, I’m going to have my masters done and then I’ll see if I go back home or if I stay, it will depend on the job opportunities. I’d like to travel, yes I would, but I don’t know if it will be possible or not.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Are you going to do your masters here?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Erm, I’m deciding, I don’t know if I’m going to stay here in the UK, not in this university, but in the UK or Spain. I’m not sure yet.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Are there many universities that do your course?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Er in UK, yeah I think so. In London and in England actually.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok, do you think that the career prospects are good in your area? Are there lots of job opportunities?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: I think it will be difficult at first. It’s like I don’t imagine me going and finding a beautiful job at first, but er I’ll have to fight and work really hard.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Are you happy with all the career choices you’ve made so far? If you did it all over again would you do anything differently?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Perhaps not going to sound technology but media technology as I’ve found out it’s what I like the most. But I like sound as well, but I prefer video. But yeah, I think I’m happy with my choices.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: You seem enthusiastic about it. If you had to describe the culture or characteristics of your industry, what five words would you use?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Erm, it’s a male industry, er I think competitive. It’s dynamic I think, I like that. I don’t know.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: What do you think it is about it that makes it a male industry?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: I don’t know, I think its because until now, we only see, it’s not we only see, but most of the time we only see men working and that’s why we connect it to, we say it’s a male industry, because we see more men than women working on it.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Do you think that the fact its so male dominated will cause you any problems at all in the future?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: I think if I wanted to work in sound I’d have more problems than on the video part. I think, I’m not sure because I’ll only see after I’m in the industry, I think so, yeah.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: My last question is, do you think that your educational experiences differ from other students say in social sciences or humanities?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: I think this university has a very good practical side of the course, all courses have a very good practical side. Actually I have some friends studying sciences and they usually go to the labs as well, so I think its similar, I don’t know.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok that’s everything. Thank you very much for your help.
